image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Approach above the observed red hub with open fingers and level downward hand; estimate its center from current head view.
Center over the red hub and descend toward grasp height, keeping fingers open for visual alignment.
Lower the last 8 mm around the hub, correct a small lateral offset, then close progressively to grasp.
Lift vertically while maintaining hub grip; check that the red gear rises and remains centered between both fingers.
Red gear is retained above the table. Carry it toward the empty base peg at clearance height, then inspect centering before insertion.
Make a small lateral centering correction from wrist/base alignment and lower the held gear slowly toward the peg.
The held hub appears vertically aligned over the peg. Lower straight down in small increments while preserving the grasp.
The gear tilted during descent, suggesting peg-edge contact rather than insertion. Back upward to unload and inspect its retention and alignment.
Previous tensor was rejected with no motion. Correct the malformed rotation entry; make a small centering correction and partial descent from the unchanged observation.
Continue a slow vertical insertion at the corrected center, watching for renewed tilt or sliding in the fingers.
The hub again shifts and tilts before seating. Unload upward, then correct along the wrist-view depth direction toward the estimated peg center.
Retry the vertical insertion after the depth correction, using 1 mm steps and retaining the hub.
No motion occurred in the rejected chunk. Correct the rotation entry, unload vertically, and make the intended small horizontal centering adjustment.
Lower toward seating at the newly centered position; monitor whether the hub stays level relative to the fingers.
Insertion remains uncertain and the hub has shifted. Lift and move clear to expose the peg for a fresh visual alignment rather than pushing farther.
Return over the exposed peg with a small lateral correction for the hub's offset in the fingers, remaining above contact.
Correct the slight visible lateral hub-to-peg offset and descend to just above the previous contact height.
Try a small yaw adjustment during slow descent to resolve possible tooth interference; watch for tilt rather than assuming seating.
The hub tilts toward the wrist on contact. Unload and shift 5 mm along the depth direction to test the suspected peg-edge offset.
Retry descent after the depth correction, preserving the yaw and grip so any renewed hub tilt is visible.
The gear is contacting the peg but still tilting. Ease the fingers open at this low height so it can self-center and settle; inspect before regrasping.
Clear the fingers upward with a wider opening to see whether the gear settles onto the peg independently.
The released gear is level but appears perched above its seated height. Regrasp its now-visible hub before a small peg-centering adjustment.
Unload the perched gear, shift a few millimeters toward the estimated peg center from the visible hub position, then approach contact again.
Correct the rejected tensor from the unchanged pose. Unload and test a nearby center farther back along the depth direction.
Test seating at the revised depth alignment with a slow, straight descent.
Unload the tilted gear and correct the lateral peg estimate using the visible pin height; shift toward the lower-y side before retrying.
Lower vertically at the revised center and assess peg entry from the gear's motion relative to the hand.
The previous tensor was rejected without motion. Correct it to lift clear and test a farther forward center, with no unintended rotation.
Approach at the farther-forward alignment, adding a small lateral correction from the head-view vertical projection.
The gear is lower and the peg may be entering the bore. Ease the grip slightly and apply a small seating twist while descending only 6 mm.
Correct the rejected tensor from the unchanged pose: lift, then move aside with no rotation to expose the peg.
Return above the exposed peg and ease the grasp near contact, allowing a little self-centering instead of rigidly forcing insertion.
With the gear supported near the peg and the fingers eased, make a small shallow depth sweep to encourage the bore to settle over the pin.
Re-establish a light hub grasp and combine a small lateral adjustment with a seating twist, allowing only a shallow descent.
Reset the grasp around the perched hub at a slightly higher, recentered hand pose; the previous light grasp was sliding rather than carrying the gear reliably.
Correct the rejected tensor: no motion occurred. Lift with the reset grasp and shift toward the peg with zero rotation.
Lower the securely held gear at the revised center toward the seated height; inspect whether the bore enters without tilting.
The gear is near engagement height but tilted. Hold height and apply a gradual seating turn with a slightly eased grip to resolve tooth or peg interference.
Release the low, turned gear and clear upward slightly to let it settle independently and inspect whether it is seated on the peg.
